cards.title: A pixel that isn’t working
cards.label: flagged
evidence: Flagged by the pipeline as permanently unusable (NONFUNC) and as a jump during the exposure (TRANSIENT)
About 23,052 MJy/sr in one pixel, about 58,170 times its neighbours (about 0.4)
Nothing there in 18 of 18 other photos of the same sky within 5 days
cards.howToTell: A real source stays with the sky, so it shows in other photos of the same spot. A bad pixel stays with the detector, so other photos of the same spot don’t show it.

cards.title: Cosmic ray or one-off glitch
cards.looksLike: a new source that appears once
cards.label: flagged
evidence: Flagged by the pipeline as a jump during the exposure (TRANSIENT), over 4 pixels, a typical size for a cosmic-ray hit
The pipeline also flags a ring of pixels around each hit (HALO)
Nothing there in 3 of 3 other photos we have of that spot, within 5 days
No known source or asteroid at that place
cards.howToTell: Something that shows in one photo and in none of the others of the same spot, minutes to days apart, isn’t a new object in the sky.

cards.title: An afterglow on the detector
cards.label: flagged
evidence: Flagged as an afterglow (PERSIST): the pipeline’s flag for light left on the detector by something bright it saw before
Nothing there in 15 of 15 other photos of the same sky within 5 days
The earlier photo that left it isn’t among the photos we have, so the bright source itself can’t be shown
cards.howToTell: If it isn’t in the other photos of the same spot and carries a persistence flag, it’s the detector remembering, not the sky.

cards.title: A star too bright for the detector
cards.looksLike: a strange blob or a spike
cards.label: confirmed
evidence: Barnard’s Star, Gaia DR3 G 8.2: far brighter at its centre than SPHEREx can measure
Flagged at its centre as saturated (BLOOM, OVERFLOW; 84 pixels)
Its light is real; only the centre’s numbers can’t be trusted
cards.howToTell: A blob on a bright catalogued star with saturation flags is the star itself, not something new.

panels.caption: outlined: saturation (BLOOM, OVERFLOW)
panels.alt: Barnard's Star: the saturated centre outlined

cards.title: An ordinary star (for comparison)
cards.label: confirmed
evidence: S/N 50; no artefact flags; no other Gaia star within 3 pixels
Seen in all 54 other photos of the same spot; in the one shown, S/N 51, its light spread over 5 pixels, as a star's is
cards.howToTell: A catalogued star that shows in every photo of the spot is just a star.

cards.title: Two sources in one pixel
cards.looksLike: one object, maybe a new one
cards.label: confirmed
evidence: On 1 May 2026, WISE 0855’s predicted place and a Gaia star (G 16.3) are 6.4″ apart, about one SPHEREx pixel (6.15″); in November 2025 they were 9.5″ apart, because WISE 0855 moves
From the short colour to the long one, the light moves off the star, towards WISE 0855’s place
Light centre: within 0.7″ of the star at 1.1–1.6 µm; 3.5″ from it and 2.9″ from WISE 0855 at 4.4–5 µm (centres good to about 1″)
cards.howToTell: If a catalogued star sits within a pixel or two, the spot is a blend: look at its colours, as “Two colours” does on WISE 0855’s page.
